# Technical Excellence

Create solutions that are simple, maintainable, readable, and appropriate for the problem being solved.

---

## Principles

- [Simplicity Over Complexity](../principles/simplicity-over-complexity.md) — optimise for understanding, not cleverness
- Build for today's requirements — avoid speculative architecture
- Optimise for maintainability — every system should be understandable by someone joining tomorrow
- Manage technical debt intentionally — visible, documented, deliberately accepted

---

## Coding Standards

Consistency and readability matter more than personal preference.

- Consistent style across the codebase
- Meaningful, descriptive naming
- Small, focused functions with clear purpose
- Minimal duplication
- Clear abstraction boundaries

See → [Python Standards](../standards/python-standards.md), [SQL Standards](../standards/sql-standards.md)

---

## Code Reviews

Reviews exist for knowledge sharing, risk reduction, and consistency — not gatekeeping.

- Keep PRs small and focused
- Review intent before implementation
- Focus areas: correctness, readability, security, performance, testability

See → [Pull Request Guidelines](../delivery/pull-request-guidelines.md)

---

## Definition of Done

Work is complete only when:

- Code is merged
- Tests pass
- Documentation is updated
- Monitoring is in place
- Security checks pass
- Acceptance criteria are met

See → [Definition of Done](../delivery/definition-of-done.md)

---

## Strong Signals

- Clear architecture with consistent patterns
- Low complexity, high readability
- Minimal duplication
- Good abstraction boundaries

## Weak Signals

- Overengineering or excessive abstraction
- Hidden dependencies
- Large, fragile components
- Clever but hard-to-understand solutions
